content:
The image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, circular-to-oval, orange/cinnamon-red pustules densely packed across the upper leaf surface. The pustules are small, round, and appear almost exclusively on the upper surface. There is also a pale/white streak running along the leaf, possibly from a prior injury.

Key observations:
- Small, circular, densely packed pustules
- Orange to cinnamon-red color
- Located predominantly on the upper leaf surface
- More circular and densely packed than common rust

This matches **Southern_Rust** — pustules that are smaller, more circular, more densely packed than common rust, and found almost exclusively on the upper leaf surface with light orange to cinnamon-red urediniospores.

Common rust would have darker reddish-brown, more elongated pustules on both surfaces. The circular shape and upper-surface predominance point to Southern rust.
